messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Serving runtime crashloop detected on cluster-gpu-eu-west (priority: P1). 3 pods in crashloopBackOff in namespace=redwood-serving. Root hinted: SIGSEGV in runtime-engine v2.1.4.

alex: saw the page, pulling logs now. give me 1–2 min. :coffee:

maria: tagging for visibility — customers in eu-west might be impacted. I’m checking active routes.

alex: logs from pod runtime-engine-5d7f:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] runtime: starting model=redwood-open-13b
[2026-03-15T10:12:12Z] gpu0: load model shards
[2026-03-15T10:12:14Z] ERROR: segfault (signal 11) at 0x7fffb3a2
stack: engine::kernel_dispatch()+0x2f 
*** SIGSEGV (core dumped) ***
```

alex: crash repeats after container restarts, immediate OOMs not obvious — looks like kernel-level fault (custom fused-kernel/TensorRT path). 3 pods across 2 nodes.

dmitri: attaching an strace/core isn’t trivial on crashloop but we can collect last-core from /var/lib/kcore if available. kubectl describe shows CrashLoopBackOff
```
Events:
  BackOff  2m (x5 over 5m) kubelet back-off restarting failed container
```

julie: customer-impact: I see elevated 5xx rates on /v1/generate for eu-west routes. Approximately 12 customers with active calls in the last 10m. Notifying CS to throttle or failover.

oncall-rotation: alex (now) -> maria (handoff in 20m). maria, take lead if alex needs break.

alex: mitigation plan in-flight: 1) scale down replicas for affected model to 0 to stop immediate churn and reduce noise 2) pin traffic to backup variant (redwood-open-13b-quant) via routing policy 3) collect core + full journalctl on affected nodes 4) enable engine fallback: RUNTIME_DISABLE_CUSTOM_KERNELS=1 on a test pod.

maria: executing step 1 (scale down) now: `kubectl scale deploy/runtime-open-13b --replicas=0 -n redwood-serving` — done. Stopping restart spam.

alex: routing change applied: all eu-west traffic shifted to redwood-open-13b-quant (CPU-quantized variant) using canary rule. Confirmed lower error rate on health checks.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Route update deployed by alex at 2026-03-15T10:16:08Z. 0/3 errors on new variant (rolling).

dmitri: spun up one isolated debug pod with `RUNTIME_DISABLE_CUSTOM_KERNELS=1` to replicate. Starting under gdb. If the segfault is in TRT fused-kernel, disabling custom kernels should avoid it.

julie: notifying top-affected customers with a brief: "We're aware of intermittent 5xx from eu-west and have routed traffic to a fallback model. Engineers are investigating root cause. We may have degraded latency. We'll update in 30m." Sent.

alex: collecting core dumps: `/var/lib/crash/core.runtime-engine.*` copying to s3://redwood-incidents/1867890123/ then will run `europetest:core-analyzer` to get a first-pass symbolized stack.

maria: I’m going to cordon node-gpu-12 that had 2 crashlooping pods to prevent more scheduling while we debug: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-12`. Doing drain next if safe.

dmitri: quick triage: kernel traces show GPU driver messages immediately before SIGSEGV: `E | nvidia 0000:xx:xx: memory access fault` — suspicious driver/kernel/kernel ABI combo. We need to check recent infra churn: any node rollouts in last 12h?

alex: infra says a GPU driver upgrade landed 6h ago on eu-west. I'll open a rollback candidate and flag infra oncall.

oncall-rotation: infra-oncall @derek please advise on driver rollback plan.

ops-bot: :information_source: mitigation summary: replicas scaled down, traffic pinned to quantized fallback, debug pod with custom kernels disabled created, node-gpu-12 cordoned. Customer notice sent.

ajex: (typo) — ignore

maria: handoff note for next oncall: monitor for residual 5xx on eu-west, verify client retries, follow-up with infra about driver rollback window, preserve cores and logs at s3://redwood-incidents/1867890123. Postmortem owner: alex.

alex: next steps: 1) if fallback continues stable for 15m, begin controlled rollout: bring 1 replica of primary with env var `RUNTIME_DISABLE_CUSTOM_KERNELS=1` and confirm stability, 2) coordinate driver rollback with infra and test on a single node, 3) prepare postmortem with root-cause hypotheses (TRT fused-kernel + driver mismatch) and remediation (pin driver, add kernel guards, and enable safer rollout for driver upgrades).

maria: acknowledging. I'll take next 20m watch and will escalate to SE if customer impact shifts.

incidents-bot: Incident P1 escalated: active, assigned alex, severity P1 -> ongoing. Reminder: create incident ticket and timeline.

alex: creating incident ticket now: INC-2026-186789. Saving timeline and attaching logs.

julie: updating customers channel with CIR status. Will loop back when rollback/patch decision made. :eyes:

end of thread.
